_meta.description: New York courts, agencies, and federal forums for JARVIS triage routing.
_meta.note: Every entry needs verification against current official sources before use.

courts.name: New York Supreme Court
courts.description: General jurisdiction trial court. Handles civil cases above lower court limits, matrimonial actions, and Article 78 proceedings against government agencies.

courts.name: New York City Civil Court
courts.description: Handles civil cases in NYC with claims up to $50,000. Includes a Housing Part and a Small Claims Part.
courts.notes: Only exists in NYC. Outside NYC, equivalent is City Court or District Court.

courts.name: New York City Housing Court
courts.description: Part of NYC Civil Court. Handles landlord-tenant disputes including evictions, repairs, and housing code violations in NYC.
courts.notes: Outside NYC, landlord-tenant cases go to City Court, District Court, Town Court, or Village Court.

courts.name: Small Claims Court (NYC)
courts.description: Part of NYC Civil Court. Claims up to $10,000 for individuals, $5,000 for businesses. Informal procedures, no lawyer needed.
courts.notes: Outside NYC, small claims are part of City Court, District Court, Town Court, or Village Court. Limits may differ.

courts.name: Family Court
courts.description: Handles custody, visitation, child and spousal support, family offense (orders of protection), paternity, adoption, guardianship, foster care, juvenile delinquency, and PINS. Does NOT handle divorce (that is Supreme Court).
courts.notes: Divorce and annulment must be filed in Supreme Court. Family Court handles almost everything else family-related.

courts.name: Surrogate's Court
courts.description: Handles probate of wills, estate administration, guardianship of property, and trust matters. One per county.

courts.name: New York City Criminal Court
courts.description: Handles misdemeanors and violations in NYC. Felonies are arraigned here but tried in Supreme Court.
courts.notes: Outside NYC, criminal cases go to County Court (felonies), City Court, District Court, Town Court, or Village Court.

courts.name: County Court
courts.description: Outside NYC: handles felony criminal cases, civil cases over lower court limits, and some appeals from lower courts. One per county (57 counties outside NYC).
courts.notes: Does not exist in NYC. NYC equivalent for felonies is Supreme Court.

courts.name: District Court
courts.description: Exists only in Nassau County and western Suffolk County. Handles civil cases up to $15,000, small claims up to $5,000, misdemeanors, and landlord-tenant.

courts.name: City Court
courts.description: In cities outside NYC (61 cities). Handles civil up to $15,000, small claims up to $5,000, misdemeanors, violations, and some landlord-tenant. Comparable to NYC Civil Court.

courts.name: Town and Village Justice Court
courts.description: Nearly 1,300 courts across NYS outside cities. Handle vehicle and traffic offenses, small claims up to $3,000, misdemeanors, violations, and some civil matters. Often the first court a person encounters outside urban areas.

courts.name: Court of Claims
courts.description: Hears claims for money damages against the State of New York. Claims against the state cannot be brought in other courts.

agencies.name: New York State Workers' Compensation Board
agencies.description: Adjudicates workers' compensation claims. District offices across NYS. Employer must be notified within 30 days; claim filed within 2 years of injury.
agencies.notes: Not a court. Administrative agency with its own hearing process. No county choice — assigned by district.

agencies.name: New York State Department of Labor
agencies.description: Administers unemployment insurance benefits. Initial claims filed online or by phone. Also handles wage theft complaints.

agencies.name: Unemployment Insurance Appeal Board
agencies.description: Hears appeals from ALJ decisions on unemployment insurance claims. First appeal goes to an Administrative Law Judge; second appeal to this Board.

agencies.name: New York State Division of Human Rights
agencies.description: Investigates and adjudicates discrimination complaints under the NY Human Rights Law. Covers employment, housing, public accommodations, and credit discrimination.

agencies.name: NYC Commission on Human Rights
agencies.description: Enforces NYC Human Rights Law. Handles discrimination in employment, housing, and public accommodations within NYC. Often broader protections than state or federal law.

agencies.name: NYC Comptroller's Office — Claims Division
agencies.description: Receives Notice of Claim filings against New York City agencies. Required within 90 days of incident for tort claims against the city.

agencies.name: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs
agencies.description: Administers veterans benefits including disability compensation, pension, education (GI Bill), and healthcare. Initial claims filed with VA regional offices.

agencies.name: Board of Veterans' Appeals
agencies.description: Hears appeals of VA benefit decisions. Veterans can request a direct review, submit new evidence, or request a hearing.

agencies.name: U.S. Court of Appeals for Veterans Claims
agencies.description: Federal court that reviews BVA decisions. Must file within 120 days of BVA decision.

agencies.name: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services
agencies.description: Processes immigration and naturalization applications. Handles asylum applications (affirmative), work permits, green cards, citizenship.

agencies.name: Executive Office for Immigration Review (Immigration Court)
agencies.description: Immigration courts that hear removal (deportation) proceedings and asylum cases (defensive). Part of DOJ, not the judicial branch.
agencies.notes: NY immigration courts: 26 Federal Plaza (NYC), Varick St (NYC), Batavia (Western NY).

agencies.name: Board of Immigration Appeals
agencies.description: Appellate body for immigration court decisions. Must appeal within 30 days of immigration judge decision.

agencies.name: Social Security Administration
agencies.description: Administers Social Security retirement, SSI, and SSDI benefits. Disability claims go through initial review, reconsideration, ALJ hearing, Appeals Council, then federal court.

agencies.name: NYS Office of Temporary and Disability Assistance
agencies.description: Oversees public assistance (TANF/welfare), SNAP (food stamps), and Medicaid eligibility. Fair hearings available for denials or reductions.

agencies.name: Equal Employment Opportunity Commission
agencies.description: Handles federal employment discrimination charges (Title VII, ADA, ADEA). Must file before suing in federal court. NY district office at 33 Whitehall Street, NYC.

agencies.name: New York State Attorney General — Consumer Frauds Bureau
agencies.description: Investigates consumer fraud, scams, and deceptive business practices. Takes complaints but does not represent individuals.

agencies.name: New York State DMV
agencies.description: Handles license suspensions, revocations, and administrative hearings for traffic offenses. Also handles no-fault insurance disputes.

agencies.name: Traffic Violations Bureau (NYC)
agencies.description: Handles most moving traffic violations in NYC. Not a court — an administrative tribunal under DMV. No right to jury trial.
agencies.notes: Only in NYC. Outside NYC, traffic tickets go to Town/Village Justice Courts.

federal_courts.name: U.S. District Court — Southern District of New York
federal_courts.description: Federal trial court for Manhattan, Bronx, Westchester, Rockland, Putnam, Orange, Dutchess, Sullivan. Handles federal question cases, diversity cases over $75,000, immigration appeals, civil rights under 42 USC 1983, and Social Security appeals.

federal_courts.name: U.S. District Court — Eastern District of New York
federal_courts.description: Federal trial court for Brooklyn, Queens, Staten Island, Nassau, Suffolk. Same jurisdiction as SDNY for different counties.

federal_courts.name: U.S. District Court — Northern District of New York
federal_courts.description: Federal trial court covering upstate NY from Albany to the Canadian border.

federal_courts.name: U.S. District Court — Western District of New York
federal_courts.description: Federal trial court for Buffalo, Rochester, and surrounding western NY counties.
